title: Reference uniqueness, inverse conditioning and sampling cost are distinct
problem: Determine whether the unique triangle sufficient condition in R22 also guarantees stable or economical reconstruction.
failure: A unique triangle can have a uniformly separated distance signature while its known-anchor inverse gain diverges as its height tends to zero. Exact identifiability does not establish noise robustness or cheap sampling.
correction: Separate signature separation, conditional inverse conditioning and reference-event availability. For fixed known anchors (0,0),(L,0),(c,h), 0<c<L, the sharp vertical gain of the squared-distance subtraction inverse over the bounded-error cube is 1/h. Use a better-conditioned unique reference when available. In the uniform N-point, unique-triangle procedure, independent quadruples hit a specified target with the reference with probability 6/N^4; the union bound gives a sufficient sample count.
transfer: Evaluate reference selection separately for recognition, error amplification and availability. Do not interpret anchored-coordinate instability as global shape instability modulo isometries. Retain the measurement noise and sampling model when making comparisons.
limits: R23 assumes known exact labeled anchor coordinates and bounded additive squared-distance errors for its linear inverse. Ten heights and 160 exact noise-vertex checks. Rare-reference count is a sufficient bound for one independent-quadruple procedure, not a lower bound for all reconstruction methods. No full noisy-deck algorithm, physical measurement, global shape instability, optimality, independent review or originality claim.
author: TOTO
